01 · Context

The problem

Why the old calendar could double-book or book nobody.

Customers buy building and pest inspections in the company's Booking Portal, then pick an appointment time. Appointments live in Microsoft Dynamics 365, where office staff also create and move them. The portal's calendar was supposed to show when inspectors are busy, so I traced it end to end: the AngularJS page, its routes, the MVC controller and the C# service behind it.

The audit showed the calendar mostly ignored real availability. It only saw appointments where the inspector was the organizer, and the default "All Inspectors" option saved bookings with no inspector at all.

Before

  • "All Inspectors" saved OwnerId: 'all', which became an empty GUID: the appointment belonged to nobody and blocked nothing.
  • Appointments office staff created for an inspector didn't block the inspector online.
  • Any server error showed an empty calendar, which looked fully free.
  • The query had no paging, so records past 5,000 were silently dropped.
  • Drag and drop on a fixed 6 am to 6 pm FullCalendar grid, with the inspector list locked after the first product.

After

  • "All Inspectors" offers a slot only when a qualified inspector is free, and assigns that inspector automatically.
  • Inspectors are matched as organizer, attendee or owner through Dynamics 365 activity parties.
  • Failures return a 500 and the grid shows an error with a retry button, never a false free calendar.
  • Every page of results is read.
  • A click-to-book hour grid with booking hours from config, a choice summary, and a layout that works on phones.
02 · Requirements

User stories

Written from the audit findings, each with the acceptance criteria the build was checked against.

Customer
As a home buyer, I want to see which hours are free for my inspection, so that I can book a time without phoning the office.
Acceptance criteria
  • A week of days, one rectangle per hour, with the time inside each.
  • Booked, past and too-late hours can't be chosen and say why.
  • A 2-hour product highlights both hours before and after choosing.
Customer
As a customer who doesn't mind who inspects, I want to book with any qualified inspector, so that I get the widest choice of times.
Acceptance criteria
  • "All Inspectors" uses only inspectors skilled for the product.
  • A slot is open while at least one of them is free for the whole appointment.
  • A free inspector is assigned and shown in the summary.
Office staff
As office staff, I want appointments I create in Dynamics 365 for an inspector to block that inspector online, so that customers can't double-book them.
Acceptance criteria
  • Match the inspector as organizer, required or optional attendee, or owner.
  • Ignore completed and cancelled appointments.
  • Read every result page, past 5,000 records.
Operations
As the operations manager, I want the portal never to show a falsely free calendar, so that a CRM outage can't cause bad bookings.
Acceptance criteria
  • A CRM failure is logged and returns HTTP 500, not an empty list.
  • The grid shows "We couldn't load inspector availability" with Try again.
  • Slots can't be chosen until availability has loaded.
Business owner
As the business owner, I want booking hours set in one place, so that changing our day doesn't need a code change.
Acceptance criteria
  • Start hour, end hour, slot length, hidden weekdays and booking window in one config block.
  • Appointment length comes from the product, not the page.
Developer
As a developer, I want the availability query covered by fast unit tests, so that changes can be checked without a Dynamics 365 environment.
Acceptance criteria
  • A fake IOrganizationService stands in for CRM.
  • Mapping, de-duplication, paging and failure are covered.
  • Tests run in routine builds; integration tests stay separate.
03 · Design

Architecture

Three tiers on one Dataverse environment. Amber outlines mark what this work added or changed.

Added or changed in this work Test project Existing platform

One booking, end to end

  1. Browser

    The route loads the inspectors qualified for the product, then the page opens on "All Inspectors" (or the inspector chosen earlier, if qualified).

  2. Browser

    schedulingService.getInspectorAppointments posts the inspector IDs and a 3-month window as UTC times.

  3. API

    GetInspectorAppointments validates the window and calls InspectorAppointmentService; the JSON size limit is lifted for large result sets.

  4. Dynamics

    FetchXML joins appointment to activityparty: open or scheduled appointments overlapping the window, where the inspector is organizer, attendee or owner. Results are read page by page.

  5. API

    Rows come back as one record per appointment per inspector, de-duplicated, with UTC start and end times.

  6. Browser

    Busy time is merged per inspector. For "All Inspectors" the periods are intersected, so an hour is "Fully booked" only when every qualified inspector is busy.

  7. Browser

    The customer clicks an hour. The page checks the whole appointment length fits and picks the first inspector free for all of it.

  8. Dynamics

    Save posts to CreateAppointments, which creates the appointment with that inspector as organizer and owner, so it blocks them for the next customer.

05 · Build

Key code

The three pieces that decide whether a slot is free.

FetchXMLInspectorAppointmentService.cs
<!-- open (0) or scheduled (3) appointments overlapping the window -->
<fetch mapping='logical' no-lock='true' page='{0}' count='5000'>
  <entity name='appointment'>
    <filter type='and'>
      <condition attribute='statecode' operator='in'><value>0</value><value>3</value></condition>
      <condition attribute='scheduledstart' operator='lt' value='{windowEnd}' />
      <condition attribute='scheduledend' operator='gt' value='{windowStart}' />
    </filter>
    <!-- required (5), optional (6), organizer (7), owner (9) -->
    <link-entity name='activityparty' from='activityid' to='activityid' alias='ap'>
      <condition attribute='participationtypemask' operator='in'>
        <value>5</value><value>6</value><value>7</value><value>9</value>
      </condition>
      <condition attribute='partyid' operator='in'>…inspector ids…</condition>
    </link-entity>
  </entity>
</fetch>

Matching through activity parties is what lets appointments created by office staff block an inspector. The query is re-run with page 2, 3 and so on until Dynamics reports no more records.

C# endpointAppointmentController.cs
public ActionResult GetInspectorAppointments(List<Guid> inspectorIds, DateTime? fromDate, DateTime? toDate)
{
    var fromUtc = (fromDate ?? DateTime.UtcNow).ToUniversalTime();
    var toUtc = (toDate ?? fromUtc.AddMonths(3)).ToUniversalTime();
    if (toUtc <= fromUtc) { Response.StatusCode = 400; return Json("toDate must be after fromDate.", ...); }

    try
    {
        var rows = InspectorAppointmentService.QueryInspectorAppointments(GetService(), inspectorIds, fromUtc, toUtc);
        var result = Json(rows, JsonRequestBehavior.AllowGet);
        result.MaxJsonLength = int.MaxValue;   // all inspectors x 3 months can pass 2 MB
        return result;
    }
    catch (Exception)
    {
        Response.StatusCode = 500;            // never an empty list: it would look free
        return Json("Could not load inspector appointments.", ...);
    }
}
AngularJS servicescheduling.service.js
// Times when EVERY given inspector is busy. With one inspector, that's simply their busy time.
function fullyBookedPeriods(rows, inspectorIds) {
  if (!inspectorIds.length) { return []; }
  var map = busyByInspector(rows, inspectorIds);   // merged periods per inspector
  var result = null;
  for (var key in map) {
    result = result === null ? map[key] : intersectIntervals(result, map[key]);
    if (!result.length) { return []; }        // someone is always free
  }
  return result || [];
}

The same function serves both modes, so "one inspector" and "All Inspectors" can't drift apart. A sibling, findFreeInspector, picks who gets the booking.

Tasks

The work in the order it was done, then what's left before release.

1. Audit

Discovery
  • Traced availability through the AngularJS controller, template, routes and scheduling serviceFound the "All Inspectors" default, the inverted dropdown lock and the stale-drop bug.
  • Reviewed AppointmentController and AppointmentServiceOrganizer-only matching, no paging, null on error, empty-GUID owner, malformed FetchXML.

2. API

C# · Dynamics 365
  • Built InspectorAppointmentServiceFetchXML over appointment and activity parties, overlap window, de-duplication, page-by-page reads, rethrow on failure.
  • Wrote 15 xUnit tests with a hand-written fake IOrganizationServiceMapping, UTC handling, de-duplication, query shape, "all inspectors", paging and failure.
  • Added the GetInspectorAppointments endpointOptional inspector list and window, 400 on a bad window, 500 on CRM failure, large-response limit lifted.

3. Wire up

AngularJS
  • Added the API call and availability maths to schedulingServiceMerge, intersect and find-free functions, checked against sample data.
  • Reloaded the calendar whenever the inspector dropdown changesUnlocked the dropdown, ignored out-of-date responses, cleared stale selections, added the error state.
  • Assigned a real inspector for "All Inspectors" bookingsFixes appointments that were saved with no inspector.
  • Called CreateAppointments from Save, behind a temporary switchLets the calendar be tested end to end before the payment step.

4. Redesign

Template · CSS
  • Showed every inspector's bookings in "All Inspectors", with names and a colour key
  • Replaced FullCalendar drag and drop with the hour-slot gridConfig-driven hours, 8 rectangle states, multi-hour preview, choice summary, week paging, phone layout.
  • Moved the grid styles into the global styles.css using the portal's existing tokens

Next

Before release

DefectEffectFix
"All Inspectors" saved as owner 'all'Angular → Appointment modelBound to an empty GUID: appointment had no inspector and never blocked a slot.Assign the first qualified inspector free for the whole appointment.
Matched by organizer onlyAppointmentServiceAppointments created by office staff left inspectors looking free.Join activity parties: organizer, required, optional, owner.
"All" mode used every CRM userAppointmentServiceOne office user's diary shrank blocked time to almost nothing.Only inspectors qualified for the product.
"All" mode ignored skillsAngular controllerA slot showed free because an unqualified inspector was free.Use the skill-filtered inspector list.
Errors returned nullAppointmentServiceA failed lookup showed as an empty, fully free calendar.Log, rethrow, return 500; grid shows an error with retry.
No pagingAppointmentServiceRecords past 5,000 silently dropped.Read page by page until no more records.
Backslashes inside a verbatim FetchXML stringAppointmentServiceLiteral \ characters sent to Dynamics in the inspector query.Query rewritten in the new service.
Dropdown locked after the first productschedule-appointment.htmlLater products reused the first inspector, skilled or not.Disable only while availability loads.
Stale drop after changing inspectorAngular controllerSave submitted a slot that was no longer on screen.Clear the selection on every inspector change.
Conflicting hour settingsFullCalendar config08:00 overridden by 06:00; same hours for everyone.One config block: 9 am to 5 pm, hidden days, 3-month window.
Two time zones in one recordAngular controllerStartTimeText used the browser zone, StartTime used Sydney.Both saved from the same exact instant.
